subtopic: Prometheus Metrics Types (Counter, Gauge, Histogram, Summary)
question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #39: A multi-tenant Kubernetes cluster suffered widespread Pod CrashLoopBackOff and node eviction events in Observability, Telemetry & Incident Mitigation. Several critical ingress pods were repeatedly terminated with OOMKilled (Exit Code 137) during 'Prometheus Metrics Types (Counter, Gauge, Histogram, Summary)'.

### Engineering Challenge:
How should the platform team configure Kubernetes resource management and probe semantics to stabilize 'Prometheus Metrics Types (Counter, Gauge, Histogram, Summary)'?

options.text: Remove all memory and CPU resource limits so containers can consume unbounded host physical memory.
Configure liveness probes to execute an intensive 5-second database write query every 500ms.
Set explicit memory limits matching container cgroup allocations, tune JVM/runtime heap ratios (MaxRAMPercentage), and configure startup probes with sufficient failureThreshold.
Disable container restart policies by setting restartPolicy: Never across all deployments.

answer_explanation: OOMKilled exit code 137 occurs when a container breaches its cgroup memory limit. Aligning runtime heap allocation (e.g., -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75) with Kubernetes limits, accompanied by startup probes to decouple initial warm-up from liveness kills, ensures container resilience.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option C. Rationale: OOMKilled exit code 137 occurs when a container breaches its cgroup memory limit.
